grades.quote: Code in start.c (1102) sets some control bits that allow supervisor-mode access to the timer control registers, and then asks for the first timer interrupt.
grades.reason: xv6 on RISC-V notes that control bits must be set so supervisor mode can access the timer control registers (including stimecmp). It doesn't specify the actual conditions, such as the mcounteren TM bit.
This passage covers supervisor use of the time/cycle/instret counters and says timer interrupts must be schedulable. It never mentions stimecmp or the access conditions.

grades.quote: when the TM bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to access the `stimecmp` or `vstimecmp` register while executing in a mode less privileged than M will cause an illegal-instruction exception. When this bit is set, access to the `stimecmp` or `vstimecmp` register is permitted in S-mode if implemented
grades.reason: It directly states the access condition. If mcounteren.TM is clear, stimecmp access from a mode less privileged than M raises an illegal-instruction exception. If TM is set, S-mode access is permitted when the register is implemented.
This passage describes the vstimecmp CSR, which is the virtualized (VS-mode) timer register. It doesn't give conditions for non-virtualized S-mode access to stimecmp.
